title: Fable – Superfighters-inspired 2D action game
description: Desktop 2D pixel-art brawler-shooter built with Godot 4 and GDScript.

steps.title: Start
Choose engine, art toolchain and rendering baseline
steps.summary: Fixes the toolchain (Godot 4.7.2 + GDScript, Aseprite 1.3.18) and the core rendering/art conventions before any code is written.

steps.title: Data-driven content: arenas, fighters, weapons
steps.summary: Splits the game into a thin main scene plus content that is added as scenes/resources: self-contained arena scenes, one Fighter scene configured by CharacterData, one Weapon scene configured by WeaponData, and projectiles spawned into the arena.

steps.title: Controllers drive fighters; firearm slot with half-circle aim
steps.summary: Fighters no longer read Input. A FighterController (idle base, LocalController with per-player action prefix; bot and network controllers later) fills move/aim/jump/attack intent that the Fighter polls each physics frame. The fighter gains slot state; the firearm slot draws the weapon only while standing, aims with W/S within the facing half-circle and fires along that direction.

steps.title: Health, projectile hits and hit reactions
steps.summary: Adds a Health component node on every Fighter. Projectiles now collide with the fighters layer, skip their shooter and call Fighter.take_hit(damage, knockback); the Fighter applies damage, knockback, a short stun and a flash. On death the body leaves the fighters layer so projectiles pass through it.

steps.title: Fighter classes and data-driven melee combos
steps.summary: Characters now point to a FighterClass resource that defines how they fight. A class holds a melee combo (array of MeleeAttack resources with damage, knockback, stun, wind-up/active/recovery timing and hitbox) plus a combo cooldown. A Melee component on the Fighter runs the chain and finds targets with a physics shape query.

steps.title: Knockdown, invulnerable get-up, disarm and jump kick
steps.summary: MeleeAttack gains knocks_down; combo finishers and the new per-class air attack (jump kick, once per jump) use it. A knocked-down fighter lies down for the class's knockdown_time, is invulnerable while down and briefly after getting up, and drops its firearm into the arena as a DroppedWeapon rigid body.

steps.title: Class stats and new controller intents (run, down, combo break)
steps.summary: FighterClass now also owns movement stats (walk/run, jump, dive, roll) and max health; Fighter reads them instead of its own exports. Controllers gain run, down and combo_break intents; LocalController turns Shift/double-tap and attack+jump into them. Melee passes the attacker to take_hit so a melee stun can be broken.

steps.title: Arena weapon spawn points and pickups
steps.summary: Arenas own WeaponSpawner nodes that spawn pickable DroppedWeapons from a WeaponData list while empty. Fighters find pickable weapons with a shape query on the pickups layer: auto-take with an empty slot, swap with down when full. Weapons dropped by fighters are never pickable and expire after 5 s.

steps.title: Per-player key bindings and controls menu
steps.summary: Adds player 2 default actions and a KeyBindings helper that rewrites the pN_ actions in Godot's InputMap, saving them to user://keybindings.cfg. Main loads saved bindings on start and adds a SettingsMenu (Esc, pauses the game) to rebind keys. Fighters and LocalController are unchanged: they keep reading actions, not keys.

steps.title: Ray-traced projectiles, pellets and weighted spawns
steps.summary: Projectile changes from an Area2D to a Node2D that casts a ray along each frame's path (range, pierce, point-blank knockdown). WeaponData gains pellets, projectile_range, pierce, knockdown_range and spawn_weight, so shotgun, SMG and sniper are pure data. WeaponSpawner picks by spawn_weight. Fighter defers knockdown to the end of the frame.

steps.title: Melee items share ItemData with firearms
steps.summary: Adds an ItemData base resource (name, texture, grip, spawn weight) that WeaponData and the new MeleeItemData extend. A held MeleeItemData's combo replaces the class punches inside the Melee component, which also tracks durability and emits item_broke. WeaponSpawner and DroppedWeapon now hold any ItemData; the fighter routes a pickup to the firearm or melee slot by its data type.

steps.title: Throwables: Thrower component, thrown items and area effects
steps.summary: Slot 3 holds a counted ThrowableData (an ItemData). A Thrower component on the Fighter runs pin, fuse and throw; the thrown ThrownItem (RigidBody2D) goes off by fuse or on impact and spawns its data's effect scene: Explosion (one-off circle query) or FireArea (ticking box query on the floor). Main gives every fighter 3 grenades.

steps.title: Shared hit detection with line of sight
steps.summary: Melee, explosions and fire now find their targets through one HitQuery helper, which drops any fighter that has world geometry between the hit's origin and its body centre. Firearms also ray-check hand to muzzle so a muzzle poking past a thin wall cannot shoot through it.

steps.title: Arena root owns bounds and the match rng
steps.summary: Every arena scene's root is now an Arena script with a `bounds` rectangle and the match's RandomNumberGenerator. Fighters, thrown items and item pickups join a "bounded" group; the arena kills fighters that leave the bounds and removes items, so lost spawned items free their spawn point. Spawn picks and bullet spread draw from the arena rng.

steps.title: Inventory component; weapon pickups renamed to items
steps.summary: Slots, equipping, pickups and drops move out of Fighter into an Inventory child node (like Melee and Thrower). DroppedWeapon becomes ItemPickup and WeaponSpawner becomes ItemSpawner (scenes/items/, with ItemData and MeleeItemData), because they carry firearms, melee items and throwables alike.

steps.title: Fighter state and body size as the contract for art
steps.summary: Fighter exposes one State (IDLE ... DEAD, priority ordered) through state() and a state_changed signal, which the placeholder pose already uses and animations will follow. CharacterData gains body_size so each character's hit body matches its art; all feel settings (acceleration, friction, aim speed, crouch spread, default hit stun) move into FighterClass.

steps.title: 3x render and follow camera for large maps
steps.summary: The game renders at 1920x1080 with world units unchanged; each arena's FollowCamera follows the living fighters at art zoom 3 (one 64x96 art pixel = one screen pixel) and zooms out to 1.5 when they spread, clamped to the arena's camera_limits. CharacterData carries the art texture, pixels_per_unit 3 and the feet pixel; the fighter draws it at 1/3 scale.

steps.title: Kill credit on every hit
steps.summary: Every damage source passes its attacker to Fighter.take_hit: melee (with by_melee for the combo breaker), projectiles (shooter), explosions and fire (the thrower, set by ThrownItem.spawn_effect). The fighter remembers its last attacker for 5 s and emits died(killer), so a fall out of the map after a push is credited too. Game modes will score from this signal.

steps.title: Map-sized zoom range and mipmapped art
steps.summary: FollowCamera's furthest zoom now comes from the map: it may pull back until the whole camera_limits area fits, but never below 0.75 (character still 24 px tall at 1080p). Zoom eases in log space, fast out and calm in with a 10% start threshold. Arenas draw with linear filtering and mipmaps, and textures import with mipmaps, so zoomed-out art does not shimmer.

steps.title: Cutout rig with shared keyframe animations
steps.summary: Characters are animated as a cutout rig: each character is 11-12 part PNGs on the 64x96 canvas plus a rig.json of joint pivots and hand points. Every animation is made once as keyframe JSON (angles per part, root offset, events) on the shared rig and played on all characters; facing left is a mirror. The art AI delivers parts and keyframes per docs/CHARACTER_ANIMATION_SPEC.md; Claude imports them into Godot's Skeleton2D/AnimationPlayer and drives them from Fighter.state().

steps.title: Rig as joint nodes, built from rig.json
steps.summary: CharacterRig builds a character at runtime from rig.json and its part PNGs: one Node2D per joint, parented joint to joint, each holding its part sprite (offset so the canvas pivot sits on the joint), drawn at 1/3 scale with negative z so held items draw on top. CharacterData.rig_file selects it. Plain Node2D joints replace the planned Skeleton2D.

steps.title: Play shared keyframe clips on the cutout rig
Pick combat clips from hits and attack data
steps.summary: Melee attacks name their clip in data; the fighter reports each hit (signal plus side and stun length) so the rig animator picks flinch, fall and death clips; held melee items draw on the rig's front fist.

steps.title: Copy locomotion from mocap, draw coats as cloth
steps.summary: The clip generator reads CMU motion capture (BVH) and copies walk and crouch from it; coats become deforming meshes that hang, follow the thighs, sway and stay off the floor, replacing stiff coat sprites.

steps.title: Street Brawler becomes the reference rig, rigs get feet
steps.summary: Clips are now generated on a new profile character with separate foot parts; CharacterRig accepts optional foot_front/foot_back.

steps.title: Docks map: generated tile arena with ladders and explosive barrels
steps.summary: First real map. The Docks arena is generated from an ASCII layout into a TileMapLayer scene (one-way catwalk tiles), with map props as their own scenes: ladders the fighter climbs, and explosive barrels that any hit sets off. Art is drawn by an Aseprite Lua script.

steps.title: Camera cuts between map-maker shots at crisp zooms
steps.summary: The follow camera no longer zooms freely. Maps place CameraShot nodes (centre + zoom 3/1.5/0.75); the camera holds the closest shot containing every living fighter, plus an implicit whole-map shot, and glides between them. Map sizes must be exactly 640x360, 1280x720 or 2560x1440.

steps.title: Stick figure drawn frame by frame
steps.summary: The players become stick figures with frame-by-frame animation. Every keyframe clip is sampled at 24 fps and each frame drawn as its own picture by a generator; Aseprite keeps the editable source; a FrameAnimator plays the strips from the fighter's state. The cutout rig stays for drawn characters but no player uses it now.

steps.title: Strike effects: hit spark and wind strips
steps.summary: Melee emits hit_landed(point, heavy); the Fighter spawns a HitSpark there. Attack clips get an untinted wind strip played by FrameAnimator behind the body.

steps.title: Set aside everything but the stick figure
steps.summary: Following the user's development order (logic, temporary visuals, combat sync, blockout, real assets, polish), the cutout rig renderer, the Docks map and all item and prop art move to DONT-OPEN/ (ignored by Godot). The stick figure's FrameAnimator stays as the only character renderer; items and props are flat placeholder boxes.

components.label: Aseprite
components.description: Source of all sprites and tilesets (.aseprite files under art/).

components.label: Sprite export
components.description: Exports tagged animations into assets/ for Godot.

components.label: Godot game
components.description: Windows desktop build; 640x360 internal resolution, integer scaling, nearest filtering.

components.label: Main scene
components.description: Loads one arena, spawns fighters at its spawn points and equips starting weapons.

components.label: Arena scene
components.description: Owns geometry, SpawnPoints and Camera2D. New map = new scene.

components.label: Fighter
components.description: Shared movement/combat body; look comes from CharacterData; weapon hangs on a Hand marker.

components.label: CharacterData
components.description: Display name and look of a character.

components.label: Weapon
components.description: Shared weapon node: sprite, cooldown, projectile spawning.

components.label: WeaponData
components.description: Fire rate, damage, auto/semi, projectile scene, muzzle offset, sprite.

components.label: Projectile
components.description: Moves straight, despawns on world hit or after its lifetime.

components.label: FighterController
components.description: Intent source polled by the Fighter: move, aim, jump, attack. Base class is idle (dummy targets).

components.label: LocalController
components.description: Keyboard player; prefix selects p1_/p2_ bindings for local multiplayer.

components.label: BotController (planned)
components.description: AI for versus-computer mode.

components.label: RemoteController (planned)
components.description: Online player's intent received over the network.

components.label: Health
components.description: max_health/current, signals damaged and died; ignores damage once dead.

components.label: FighterClass
components.description: Melee combo and combo cooldown; later class stats (speed, health).

components.label: MeleeAttack
components.description: Damage, knockback, stun, timing and hitbox of one punch/kick.

components.label: Melee component
components.description: Combo chaining, queued presses, scaled end-of-combo pause, shape-query hits once per target per attack.

components.label: DroppedWeapon
components.description: A firearm lying in the arena after a knockdown; carries its WeaponData. Pickup comes later.

components.label: WeaponSpawner
components.description: Fixed spawn point; while empty, spawns one of its WeaponData entries every interval (10 s).

components.label: KeyBindings
components.description: One key per pN_ action; rebind with swap on conflict, save, load, reset to project defaults.

components.label: SettingsMenu
components.description: Esc toggles it and pauses the tree; click a binding, press a key.

components.label: ItemData
components.description: Shared by every spawnable hand item: display name, texture, grip, spawn_weight.

components.label: MeleeItemData
components.description: Knife, bat: combo (MeleeAttack list), combo cooldown, durability.

components.label: ThrowableData
components.description: Count, fuse, breaks on impact, throw speed, bounce, effect scene.

components.label: Thrower component
components.description: Throwable slot: item, count, pin-pull, fuse in hand, throw, drop live on knockdown/death.

components.label: ThrownItem
components.description: Flies and bounces; goes off when the fuse ends or on first contact.

components.label: Explosion
components.description: One-off damage, push-away and knockdown to every fighter in range.

components.label: FireArea
components.tech: Node2D + box shape query per tick
components.description: Settles on the floor; burns everyone in it every tick, no stun.

components.label: HitQuery
components.description: fighters_in(shape, transform, from, exclude): fighters overlapping a shape with a clear line from `from`; world_hit(from, to).

components.label: Inventory component
components.description: Slot enum and active slot, firearm instance, equip_*, select_slot, update_pickup, drop_firearm, drop_all.

components.label: FollowCamera
components.description: Per-arena camera: follows fighters in Fighter.GROUP, art zoom 3, min zoom 1.5, limited to Arena.camera_limits

components.label: Window fit (main.gd)
components.description: Integer stretch while the window holds 1920x1080, fractional below

components.label: CharacterData art
components.description: texture, pixels_per_unit 3, feet pixel; drawn as a Sprite2D at 1/3 scale, never used for hits

components.label: Fighter.died(killer)
components.description: Last attacker within KILL_CREDIT_TIME (5 s), itself for a self-kill, null otherwise

components.label: Character rig
components.description: Per-character parts and rig.json; shared animations from characters/_animations/*.json

components.label: RigAnimator
components.description: AnimationPlayer added with the rig; loads assets/animations/*.json, picks a clip from Fighter.state(), scales by leg length, squashes coat parts off the floor

components.label: assets/animations/*.json
components.description: Shared keyframe clips (spec section 3.1)

components.label: tools/make_animations.gd
components.description: Generates clips from foot targets with two-bone leg IK, grounded on the floor

components.label: MeleeAttack.animation
components.description: Clip name per attack; the animator tries <name>_<combo place> first

components.label: CharacterRig.hand_anchor
components.description: Node on the front forearm, turned along it, at world scale; visual only

components.label: tools/mocap.gd
components.description: Reads BVH, forward kinematics, side-view projection

components.label: art/mocap/*.bvh
components.description: CMU Graphics Lab captures (walk, squat, crouched walk); free to use

components.label: CoatMesh
components.description: Grid over a coat part; per point: hang from the coat joint, carried by the thigh to the knee then hanging, floor pooling

components.label: Street Brawler rig
components.description: Reference rig: strict profile, capsule limbs, separate feet; drawn by tools/draw_street_brawler.lua

components.label: Docks arena generator
components.description: Builds docks.tscn and its TileSet from an ASCII layout

components.label: Map props
components.description: Ladder, Barrel, ExplosiveBarrel

components.label: CameraShot
components.description: Composed view placed by the map maker

components.label: Stick figure frame generator
components.description: Samples every clip at 24 fps, draws each frame (outlined strokes, 3/4 turn, smears), writes strips and per-frame fist data; tools/stickman.lua saves .aseprite sources and exports the strips.

components.label: Stick figure frame strips
components.description: One PNG strip and one JSON (fps, loop, reference speed, front fist per frame) per clip; .aseprite sources in art/stickman.

components.label: FrameAnimator
components.description: Picks the clip from Fighter.state() (plus dive, landing roll, roll, climb, aim pose by angle) and moves the hand anchor that carries melee items.

components.label: HitSpark
components.description: Short white burst drawn with _draw where a melee hit lands.

components.label: Wind strips (<clip>_fx.png)
components.description: Untinted white wind frames per attack clip from tools/make_stickman.gd.

components.label: DONT-OPEN/ (set aside)
components.description: Docks map, rig code (CharacterRig, RigAnimator, CoatMesh), other characters, item art, Gemini robot frames, references. Ignored by Godot.

components.label: Placeholder item and prop boxes
components.description: GradientTexture2D flat boxes the size of the old art, so grips, muzzles and pickup bodies keep their sizes.

notes.text: Test arena: one pistol spawner near the left wall. The player still starts with a pistol as a testing aid.
Projectile is now a Node2D: ray along velocity*delta each frame, mask world+fighters, excludes shooter and already-pierced bodies.
Renamed in code: DroppedWeapon -> ItemPickup, WeaponSpawner -> ItemSpawner (scenes/items/).
state_changed(state) is the hook for the AnimationPlayer/AnimationTree; stance details (crouch, aim angle, held item, combo index) are read separately.

decisions.title: Godot 4.7.2 (standard) with GDScript
decisions.why: Native 2D physics, AnimatedSprite2D and TileMapLayer cover the brief without extra dependencies; GDScript avoids the .NET runtime.
decisions.tradeoffs: GDScript is slower than C# for heavy logic, irrelevant at this game's scale.

decisions.title: Aseprite instead of LibreSprite
decisions.why: User installed Aseprite; its CLI exports sprite sheets + JSON by animation tag, which LibreSprite handles poorly.

decisions.title: Pixel rendering baseline: 640x360, 32px characters, 16px tiles
decisions.why: 640x360 scales by exact integers to 1080p (x3) and 1440p (x4), keeping pixels uniform; 32px characters match the reference style.
decisions.tradeoffs: Smaller view area than 1080p native art; deliberate for retro readability.

decisions.title: Weapons as separate sprites attached to a hand anchor
decisions.why: Many weapons are planned; drawing them into body animations would multiply art work per weapon.
decisions.tradeoffs: Needs a per-frame hand anchor so the weapon follows the body.

decisions.title: Content as Godot Resources and scenes, not code
decisions.why: Many maps, characters and weapons are planned; adding one should mean adding a .tres or .tscn, not editing core scripts.
decisions.tradeoffs: Weapons with truly unique behavior will later need an optional per-weapon scene or script hook.

decisions.title: Arena owns spawn points and camera
decisions.why: Each map can frame itself and define spawns without touching main; maps are deferred but can be dropped in later.
alternatives: Camera and spawns in main scene

decisions.title: Characters are cosmetic, stats shared
decisions.why: Matches Superfighters, where fighters differ only in look; keeps balance in one place.
decisions.tradeoffs: Per-character stats can be added to CharacterData later if wanted.

decisions.title: Controller intent objects instead of Input inside Fighter
decisions.why: Local multiplayer, online multiplayer and bots must all drive the same Fighter; intent (move/aim/jump/attack) is the common interface and is small enough to sync over the network.
alternatives: Fighter reads Input with a player index
Separate fighter subclasses per control type
decisions.tradeoffs: Fighter polls the controller explicitly to avoid one-frame-late intent from Godot's parent-before-child process order.

decisions.title: Aim as one angle mirrored by facing
decisions.why: The fighter aims only within the half-circle it faces; storing -90..90 degrees and mirroring via the Visuals flip keeps weapon rotation and projectile direction consistent.

decisions.title: Health as a separate component node
decisions.why: Keeps damage bookkeeping out of movement code (brief: separate health); can be reused by destructible objects like crates later.

decisions.title: Hits resolved by collision shapes via take_hit duck typing
decisions.why: Hit detection stays independent of sprite art; any body with take_hit (fighters now, props later) can be damaged without a shared base class.
decisions.tradeoffs: One hit shape per fighter for now; per-limb hitboxes would need hurtbox areas.

decisions.title: Characters are no longer purely cosmetic
decisions.why: The user wants classes that fight differently (fast 4-punch chains, heavy punch-punch-kick, knockdowns later). Look (CharacterData) and behaviour (FighterClass) stay separate resources so new characters reuse classes.
alternatives: Keep all fighters identical as in Superfighters
Put combat fields directly on CharacterData
decisions.tradeoffs: Balancing now spans several classes.

decisions.title: Melee hits via physics shape query during the active window
decisions.why: Immediate, deterministic and independent of sprites; no extra Area2D monitoring delay. Each target is hit at most once per attack.
decisions.tradeoffs: Hitbox data lives in MeleeAttack, so it must be kept in sync with future animations by hand.

decisions.title: End-of-combo pause scales with chain length
decisions.why: Prevents unlimited punching (user requirement) without making a single jab feel sluggish; cutting a combo short cannot be spammed for advantage.
alternatives: Pause only after the full combo

decisions.title: Invulnerability by leaving the fighters collision layer
decisions.why: Projectiles and melee shape queries already filter on the fighters layer, so dropping out of it makes downed and dead fighters unhittable without extra checks in every damage source.
alternatives: is_invulnerable() check inside every hit source
decisions.tradeoffs: A per-class flag (downed_invulnerable) keeps it reversible; if hits on the ground are allowed, the fighter stays in the layer but is never knocked down again.

decisions.title: Air attack as a separate MeleeAttack on FighterClass
decisions.why: No punches in the air; each class gets one jump kick that reuses the same timing/hitbox/knockdown data and the same Melee component, so new classes only add data.
alternatives: Air variant of every combo step
decisions.tradeoffs: Only one air move per class for now; running dive kicks may need a second entry later.

decisions.title: Disarm only on knockdown, weapon drops as a physics body
decisions.why: User rule: single punches never disarm, full combos and jump kicks do. A RigidBody2D keeps the weapon in the world for future pickups.

decisions.title: Movement stats and health live on FighterClass
decisions.why: The design says classes differ in speed, jump and health; keeping them on the class resource means a new class is one .tres file and characters stay cosmetic on top of it.
decisions.tradeoffs: Health's own default is overwritten in Fighter._ready, so Health keeps a meaningless default.

decisions.title: Input gestures are interpreted in the controller
decisions.why: Double-tap running and 'attack + jump together' are keyboard gestures; bots and remote players should send the resulting intent (run, combo_break) directly, so the Fighter only sees intent.
decisions.tradeoffs: Each controller type must produce these intents on its own.

decisions.title: take_hit carries the attacker for melee hits
decisions.why: The combo breaker must push back whoever is comboing; passing the attacker with the hit avoids searching for it.
decisions.tradeoffs: Projectiles pass no attacker, which is also what makes bullet stuns unbreakable.

decisions.title: One DroppedWeapon scene with a pickable flag
decisions.why: Spawned and dropped weapons look and fall the same; only pickability and lifetime differ (user rule: only game-spawned weapons can be picked up).
decisions.tradeoffs: The name DroppedWeapon now also covers spawned items.

decisions.title: Spawn points belong to the arena scene
decisions.why: Each map decides where and which weapons appear, so new maps need no code changes; main stays unaware of spawning.

decisions.title: Pickup found by the fighter's own shape query
decisions.why: Same pattern as melee hits: no Area2D signals, works the frame the fighter overlaps, independent of art.
alternatives: Area2D on each pickup emitting body_entered
decisions.tradeoffs: Runs a small query each frame for unarmed fighters.

decisions.title: Rebind by rewriting InputMap actions
decisions.why: LocalController already reads pN_ actions, so rebinding needs no change to controllers or fighters; project.godot stays the source of defaults.
alternatives: Controller holds its own key table
decisions.tradeoffs: One key per action for now (no secondary bindings or gamepads).

decisions.title: Static helper instead of an autoload
decisions.why: Bindings are global InputMap state already; a static class avoids a singleton and works in headless test scripts, where autoloads are not guaranteed.
decisions.tradeoffs: save_path is a static var that tests override.

decisions.title: Conflicting key swaps bindings
decisions.why: Two players share one keyboard; swapping guarantees every action keeps a key and no key drives two actions.

decisions.title: Projectiles ray-trace their path instead of using Area2D overlap
decisions.why: The sniper bullet moves 25 px per frame, more than a fighter is wide; Area2D overlap would skip fighters and thin walls. A ray per frame also gives the exact hit point for range-based knockdown and lets one bullet pierce several fighters in order.
decisions.tradeoffs: Bullets are points (no width); a ray query per bullet per frame.

decisions.title: New weapon behaviour as WeaponData fields
decisions.why: Pellets, range, pierce and knockdown range cover shotgun, SMG and sniper with no per-weapon code, keeping weapons content-only.
decisions.tradeoffs: WeaponData grows; truly unique weapons (bazooka, flamethrower) may still need their own projectile scene.

decisions.title: Weighted spawns via spawn_weight on WeaponData
decisions.why: User chose weighted spawns (rare sniper, common pistol/SMG); the weight belongs to the weapon so every arena reuses it.
decisions.tradeoffs: Arenas cannot make one weapon rarer only on their map.

decisions.title: Knockdown applied deferred
decisions.why: A point-blank shotgun blast hits with 5 pellets in one frame; an immediate knockdown would make the target invulnerable after the first pellet.
decisions.tradeoffs: The knockdown state starts at the end of the frame.

decisions.title: Common ItemData base for firearms and melee items
decisions.why: Spawners, pickups and drops only need the name, sprite, grip and spawn weight, so one base lets one spawner list and one DroppedWeapon scene handle both kinds without per-kind copies.
alternatives: Separate spawner and pickup scenes per kind
decisions.tradeoffs: The fighter branches once on the data type to pick the slot; a new slot kind (throwables) adds one branch.

decisions.title: Held item lives in the Melee component, not a separate weapon node
decisions.why: A melee item is only a different combo plus durability; the existing combo runner, shape-query hits, escape pause and placeholder all work unchanged when the combo source switches.
alternatives: A MeleeWeapon node like the firearm Weapon
decisions.tradeoffs: The item's sprite is a plain Sprite2D on the hand; swing animations come later.

decisions.title: A worn-out item breaks only when its combo ends
decisions.why: Swapping the combo array mid-chain would break indexing and cut a combo the player already started.
alternatives: Break on the last hit and cancel the combo
decisions.tradeoffs: The last combo can land a hit or two past the durability.

decisions.title: The thrown item's effect is a scene named in the data
decisions.why: Grenade and molotov share the throw and flight; only what happens when they go off differs. Pointing ThrowableData at an effect scene lets mines, C4 or new bombs reuse the same flight code by adding a scene and a .tres.
alternatives: An enum of effects in code
decisions.tradeoffs: Effect tuning (radius, damage) lives on the effect scene, not the .tres; a stronger grenade variant needs its own effect scene.

decisions.title: Effects hit with shape queries on the fighters layer
decisions.why: Same as bullets and melee: independent of art, and invulnerable (downed, rolling) fighters are skipped for free because they leave the layer.
decisions.tradeoffs: Walls do not block blasts or fire yet.

decisions.title: Thrower is its own component like Melee
decisions.why: Keeps the pin, fuse and count state out of the already large Fighter script; the fighter only passes intent and the hand position.
alternatives: Fields and logic directly on Fighter
decisions.tradeoffs: Fighter still decides when the item is drawn and when to drop it live.

decisions.title: One query helper with a line-of-sight ray per target
decisions.why: Large multi-floor maps are planned; blasts, fire and melee went through walls and floors, and four copies of the same shape query would each need the wall rule.
decisions.tradeoffs: One extra ray per candidate target (a handful per hit); the target point is the body centre, so a fighter mostly hidden behind cover with its centre exposed is still hit.

decisions.title: Bounds checked centrally by the arena
decisions.why: Large maps with pits are planned; nothing died or was removed when falling out, and each mover checking its own bounds would couple it to arena data.
alternatives: Kill-zone Area2D placed by hand in each map
Each node checks a global kill height
decisions.tradeoffs: One group walk per physics frame; a rectangle cannot describe irregular map shapes (a kill-zone area can be added later).

decisions.title: One seedable rng per match
decisions.why: Replays, deterministic tests and online sync need every random roll to come from one seedable source.
decisions.tradeoffs: Nodes outside an arena fall back to a shared unseeded rng.

decisions.title: Split inventory from Fighter by job
decisions.why: fighter.gd mixed movement, aiming, firing, slots, pickups and drops (475 lines); the project rule keeps movement, combat and weapons separate.
alternatives: Split the Fighter into a state machine of nodes
decisions.tradeoffs: Callers write fighter.inventory.X; Fighter keeps firing and aiming because they depend on its stance.

decisions.title: One priority-ordered state instead of animators reading eight flags
decisions.why: Stun, knockdown, roll, dive, crouch, attack, cooking and death were separate flags; an animator re-deriving their priority would disagree with gameplay.
decisions.tradeoffs: The enum is derived each frame, not a driver of behaviour; adding a behaviour means adding its state to the order.

decisions.title: Render 1920x1080 at camera zoom 3 instead of rescaling the world
decisions.why: The user's 64x96 art and large maps need detail without retuning every speed, range and hitbox; keeping world units and drawing art at 1/3 scale leaves all gameplay numbers and tests unchanged.
decisions.tradeoffs: Zooming out below 3 shows the art smaller than 1:1; item and tile art must also come at 3x. Integer scaling crops smaller windows, so the window switches to fractional stretch below 1920x1080.

decisions.title: Credit the last hitter within a 5 s window, kept on the victim
decisions.why: All five agreed modes score kills; falls out of the map have no damage source, so the victim must remember who last hit it. Keeping it on the fighter means one signal covers every way to die.
alternatives: Track damage per attacker and credit the top damage dealer
A central damage log in the match/mode layer
decisions.tradeoffs: The last hitter can steal a kill with a small hit; assists are not tracked. The combo breaker now needs an explicit by_melee flag because the attacker is passed on every hit.

decisions.title: Furthest zoom = whole map, floored at 0.75; smooth mipmapped downscaling
decisions.why: The user wants Superfighters-style big maps where every fighter stays visible and the whole picture scales together. Fitting the map makes every fighter visible on maps up to 2560x1440 world px; the 0.75 floor keeps characters readable. Nearest filtering drops pixels when shrinking 3x art and shimmers while the zoom moves; a side-by-side render showed mipmaps blend cleanly and match nearest at zoom 3.
alternatives: Fixed min zoom per map tuned by hand
Integer-only zoom steps (3, 2, 1) with nearest filtering
Render the world to a SubViewport and downsample
decisions.tradeoffs: Art at in-between zooms is slightly soft instead of crisp; maps bigger than 2560x1440 can leave fighters off screen; every texture needs mipmaps (more memory, negligible at this art size).

decisions.title: Cutout rig instead of frame-by-frame sprite sheets
decisions.why: 20 characters (more planned) times about 67 animations would be thousands of hand frames, and AI-drawn frames drift between frames. A shared rig needs about 12 parts per character, keeps every frame consistent, matches attack timing exactly, and adding a character needs no new animation work.
alternatives: Frame-by-frame base body with clothing overlays per frame
decisions.tradeoffs: Rotated pixel art is slightly soft at the joints; the cutout look is less hand-crafted. Can be baked to sprite sheets later if needed.

decisions.title: Node2D joint hierarchy instead of Skeleton2D
decisions.why: The parts are rigid sprites that only rotate at joints; Skeleton2D adds value only for deforming meshes. Node2D joints are animated by AnimationPlayer rotation tracks the same way and keep the rig a few lines of code.
alternatives: Skeleton2D with Bone2D and Polygon2D skins
decisions.tradeoffs: No mesh bending at joints (rounded joint caps in the art cover it); no built-in IK, so two-handed aiming will need a small solver later.

decisions.title: Clip names live in attack data, hit details on the fighter
decisions.why: New weapons and classes get their animation by naming a clip in the resource, with no animator code; the animator stays cosmetic and only reads fighter state.
alternatives: Map attack display names to clips in the animator
Pass hit details through the state_changed signal
decisions.tradeoffs: Two small fighter fields exist only for animation; a missing clip falls back to idle silently.

decisions.title: Draw held melee items on the rig hand, drop them from the old marker
decisions.why: The knife and bat must follow the swing; hit detection never used the sprite, so only the art moves.
alternatives: Move the Hand marker every frame to the rig hand
decisions.tradeoffs: Firearms and throwables still draw at the old marker until their aim clips exist.

decisions.title: Copy human motion from motion capture instead of hand-posing
decisions.why: The user rejected the hand-made walk and crouch as anatomically wrong; real captures give correct timing, bob, foot paths and lean.
decisions.tradeoffs: Captures must be scaled and limited to the rig (no ankle, knee bend capped); a real walk is far slower than the game's walk speed, an open gameplay question.

decisions.title: Coats as deforming Polygon2D grids
decisions.why: A stiff coat picture rotated with the thighs stuck out like a plank and flew up in the air; a grid bends over the legs and hangs from the hips with no new art.
alternatives: Split the coat into more stiff parts
decisions.tradeoffs: A few hundred points per coat updated per frame on the CPU; no self-collision.

decisions.title: One reference skeleton for all characters
decisions.why: Shared clips only fit rigs with the same pivots; a rig-friendly profile character with feet removes the 3/4 and stiff-coat problems of character 01.
alternatives: Keep tuning the trench coat rig
decisions.tradeoffs: The trench coat agent no longer fits the clips exactly; new characters should reuse the brawler's pivots.

decisions.title: Generate the map from an ASCII layout into a TileMapLayer
decisions.why: TileMapLayer cell data is binary and cannot be written by hand; a layout string is readable, diffable and picks edge tiles from neighbours. The output is a normal scene the editor can open.
alternatives: Hand-placed StaticBody rectangles with tiled sprites
decisions.tradeoffs: The generator is the source of truth: hand edits to docks.tscn are lost on the next run.

decisions.title: Ladders climbed with world collision off, found through a node group
decisions.why: Climbing through one-way catwalks without collision is the simplest correct movement; a group plus a rect check needs no physics layer or signals.
alternatives: Area2D ladders on a new physics layer
decisions.tradeoffs: Ladders must never pass solid ground, or a fighter letting go inside it would be stuck.

decisions.title: Explosive barrels sit on the world and fighters layers
decisions.why: Bullets, melee, blasts and fire all find targets on the fighters layer, so every hit source sets a barrel off and blasts chain with no new code paths. HitQuery now skips the target's own shape on its line-of-sight ray.
alternatives: A separate hittable-props layer every hit source also queries
decisions.tradeoffs: Anything that assumes the fighters layer holds only Fighter must use duck typing (take_hit/center).

decisions.title: Shots at fixed zooms instead of a free follow zoom
decisions.why: The user wants maps made with care: every view the player sees is a composed picture, and the 3x art only shrinks by whole factors (1:1, 2:1, 4:1), which match mipmap levels and stay crisp. Large maps and the every-fighter-on-screen rule are kept.
alternatives: Single fixed screen per map (rejected by the user as too basic)
decisions.tradeoffs: Map makers must place shots; the view moves in glides between shots rather than tracking continuously. Map sizes are limited to three exact sizes.

decisions.title: Frame-by-frame strips generated from the existing keyframe clips
decisions.why: The user asked for stick figures animated frame by frame with dense, detailed motion. Sampling the existing clips reuses the mocap walk and every attack, reaction and knockdown, while each frame is a real picture that can be hand-edited in Aseprite.
alternatives: Draw the stick figure live from the rig each frame (no frames to edit)
Hand-draw every frame in Aseprite (slow, needs the user)
Keep the cutout rig with stick-figure parts
decisions.tradeoffs: Frames cost texture memory (about 0.7 MB of strips) and must be regenerated after a clip changes; hand edits in the .aseprite files are overwritten by a rerun.

decisions.title: Spark via a Melee signal, drawn at runtime
decisions.why: Combat stays free of visuals: Melee only reports where a hit landed; the effect is a tiny self-freeing node, so no art or pooling is needed.
decisions.tradeoffs: Procedural look instead of hand-drawn; easy to swap for a sprite later.

decisions.title: Wind in a separate untinted strip
decisions.why: The body sprite is tinted with the character colour through self_modulate; wind drawn into it would turn blue or red. A second sprite in step with the body keeps it white.
alternatives: Draw wind into the body strip
decisions.tradeoffs: One extra strip per attack clip (15 files).

decisions.title: One renderer (frame by frame) and grey boxes until step 5
decisions.why: The user wants to work step by step from a clean base: only the stick figure prototype stays; final art comes later.
alternatives: Keep the rig renderer next to the frame animator
decisions.tradeoffs: test_animation, test_clip_anatomy and test_docks leave the suite with the code they test; the moved work is still in git under DONT-OPEN.
